audit_name: Habu AI v2 data requirements audit

requirements.evidence: 206/206 canonical rows non-empty; timestamp+GPS validated events=149
89 field-evidence nights, but these are not proven to be all operating nights
only 7 weak zero field-evidence nights; not all GPX-confirmed full surveys
strict road-time scoring available on 44/89 field-evidence nights; historical routes are reconstructed for spatial use only
available only where actual timed GPX/visit evidence exists; cannot safely fabricate for older nights
33/37 May-Jul capture nights reconstructed; 25 at 100% capture-segment coverage
Open-Meteo historical cache exists; forecast-vs-observation distinction still required for production-equivalent backtests
canonical weather/temp are incomplete and gridded weather cannot fully represent road-level fog/wetness/microclimate
not present in canonical capture master schema as a structured per-visit road×time field
not complete across 89 nights; needed to compare capture probability per unit effort
derivable on GPX nights, unavailable for most historical nights
not present as a structured canonical capture-master field; cannot infer female from size
some observations exist in broader logs/biological-reaction data, but not normalized into the canonical capture master used by v2 ranking
can be derived deterministically/proxy from timestamp; direct canonical fields are not required if timestamp is valid
v2 requirement exists; current repository has road/map data for present study area, not Amami+Okinawa regional downloadable packs
required by v2 but not represented as production mobile data package yet

reasoning: Only 150/206 capture events have GPS, so 56 historical positives cannot teach exact road location.
Strict road×time evaluation is possible on only 44/89 field-evidence nights, leaving most nights without trustworthy timed exposure/negative evidence.
True zero nights are especially weak: 7 field-evidence zeros and the hurdle report explicitly says they are not all GPX-confirmed full surveys.

Without complete search exposure, the model sees many captures but cannot reliably distinguish 'bad road/time' from 'not searched'. This is a structural identifiability problem, not something a more complex model alone can solve.

Even after testing five advanced model families on a common candidate space, the best Top100 100m±20min coverage was 16.8% (conformal_ensemble) if present in the report, supporting the view that model complexity alone is not closing the gap to 90%.

collection_priority.item: Every search night: GPX from start to finish, including zero-capture nights
Search session start/end, distance, duration, and explicit 0-capture outcome
Road condition at observation/pass: dry/damp/wet/soaked + rainfall/fog state
collection_priority.why: road-level micro-environment can vary within gridded weather
collection_priority.target: structured automatic/manual capture for every session/observation

collection_priority.item: Pre-night forecast snapshot with issue time

collection_priority.why: reproducible offline prediction and route generation
valuable for ecology and large-female impact models but secondary to core route-time accuracy

guardrails: No missing record is treated as a negative observation.
Reconstructed historical routes may support spatial learning but not fabricated passage times.
Sex is never inferred from body size.
Production-equivalent weather evaluation must use only information available at forecast issue time.
Private road names/coordinates/hotspot rankings are not emitted in this aggregate audit.
